title: JSON schema for WordPress wp-env configuration files

core.description: The WordPress installation to use. If null is specified, wp-env will use the latest production release of WordPress.

phpVersion.description: The PHP version to use. If null is specified, wp-env will use the default version used with production release of WordPress.

plugins.description: A list of plugins to install and activate in the environment.

themes.description: A list of themes to install in the environment.

port.description: The primary port number to use for the installation. You'll access the instance through the port: http://localhost:8888

config.description: Mapping of wp-config.php constants to their desired values.

mappings.description: Mapping of WordPress directories to local directories to be mounted in the WordPress instance.

phpmyadminPort.description: The port number to access phpMyAdmin.

mysqlPort.description: The port number to access MySQL.

httpsPort.description: The HTTPS port number to use for the installation. You'll access the instance through the port: https://localhost:443

sslCertPath.description: Path to a custom SSL certificate file.

sslKeyPath.description: Path to a custom SSL key file.

multisite.description: Whether to set up a multisite installation.

env.description: The key env is available to override any of the above options on an individual-environment basis.

testsPort.description: The port number for the test site. You'll access the instance through the port: http://localhost:8889

testsHttpsPort.description: The HTTPS port number for the test site. You'll access the instance through the port: https://localhost:8443

lifecycleScripts.description: Mapping of commands that should be executed at certain points in the lifecycle.

afterStart.description: Runs after wp-env start has finished setting up the environment.

afterClean.description: Runs after wp-env clean has finished cleaning the environment.

afterDestroy.description: Runs after wp-env destroy has destroyed the environment.
